sources.title: Honorary-degree recipient profile: literature degrees, Birzeit and peace-process spokesperson
sources.findings: Read the AUB honorary-degree profile. It supports BA/MA study at AUB, a University of Virginia PhD, the 1973 English-department foundation and 1991–1993 spokesperson role. Its historical present-tense PLC membership is not a verified 2026 office. It gives a 1986–1990 deanship, while other sources give 1993 or 1995; retain the agreed 1986 start and do not invent a consensus end date.

sources.title: 28 June 2008 presidential introduction: academic appointments, ministry and MIFTAH
sources.findings: Read the 28 June 2008 presidential introduction. It specifies English-literature BA/MA degrees, medieval/comparative doctoral work, department chair terms in 1973–1978 and 1981–1984, and 1996–1998 ministerial service. It says the PhD preceded the 1973 return, conflicting with PalQuest’s later thesis-completion account; no definitive doctoral year or pre-return completion is asserted. Its contemporary MIFTAH secretary-general title and PLC office are historical, not current. The reasons given for the 1998 ministerial resignation must not automatically be transplanted to the 2020 PLO resignation.

sources.title: Hanan Ashrawi biography: birth, education, parliament and civil institutions
sources.findings: Read relevant PalQuest biography passages. The precise 8 October 1946 birth in Nablus is explained separately from the family’s Ramallah origin, resolving an otherwise common birthplace confusion. It says she returned in 1973 before completing her dissertation and defended in 1981–1982, unlike AUB’s sequence; omit degree dates. It gives the deanship until 1995, unlike AUB’s 1990 and one university indexed account’s 1993. It corroborates Jerusalem/Third Way parliamentary elections, the 1996–1998 ministry and civic organisations. Its November 2020 resignation shorthand is refined using the dated WAFA statement rather than treated as the end of service. Its 2007 commission name change is distinct from foundation and operational launch.

sources.title: Board biography: 1996 and 2006 elections, first woman on PLO executive and 2020 departure
sources.findings: Read the AMAN board biography. It corroborates her being the first woman elected to the PLO Executive Committee in 2009, re-election in 2018 and departure in 2020. The Jerusalem election in 1996 and Third Way election in 2006 concern the PLC, not PNC or PLO executive seats. It identifies her contribution to ICHR, MIFTAH and AMAN; do not claim all were solely her creations or that the national commission is merely her private NGO. Civic ambitions and organisational biographies are not independent proof of policy outcomes.

sources.title: Mapping Palestinian Politics: distinctions between PNC, PLC, PLO executive and ministerial roles
sources.findings: Read the ECFR mapping profile. It distinguishes PNC, PLC and PLO executive roles and corroborates the spokesperson and ministerial periods. Its deanship-until-1995 statement is one side of an unresolved chronology; the dossier avoids choosing an unsupported end year. Its PNC statement does not revive a current PLC or executive office. The resignation and reform statement is attributed, not treated as proof of all allegations or the exclusive personal motive for leaving.

sources.publisher: Asia Pacific Forum of National Human Rights Institutions
sources.title: Palestine commission profile: 1993 founding decree and early-1994 start of activities
sources.findings: Read the APF commission profile. It clearly separates the 1993 presidential decree creating the commission, publication in the Official Gazette in 1995, and commencement of work in early 1994. The decree was issued by Arafat in the capacities specified by the source; do not inaccurately date the institution solely to 1994 or imply that the Palestinian Authority existed in the same form throughout 1993. Ashrawi’s founding role is corroborated by the other institutional biographies, not inferred solely from this commission entry.

sources.title: 9 December 2020: Abbas accepts Ashrawi’s resignation, effective at year-end
sources.findings: Read WAFA’s report dated 9 December 2020, including the resignation-statement chronology: verbal notice on 24 November, written resignation on 26 November, confirmation meeting on 8 December, acceptance on 9 December and departure effective at year-end. November sidebar or current navigation dates are not this article’s date. The public timeline uses acceptance as the dated event and explicitly preserves the later effective end of service. It does not treat 24 November as the written-submission date.

sources.title: 9 December 2020: departure announcement and call for political reform
sources.findings: Read the Reuters dispatch carried by Arab News, with Reuters byline and 9 December 2020 publication/update timestamps. It reports the intended year-end departure, political-renewal call, 2009 first election and 2018 re-election. Its earlier account of a deferred acceptance decision is not silently substituted for WAFA’s later report of acceptance that evening. The report says she did not give a specific reason for resignation; reform requests are attributed rather than asserted to be a complete causal explanation. The current site header date is not a new 2026 interview.

sources.title: 20 January 2026: women’s-affairs dialogue attended by Ashrawi as Birzeit trustees chair
sources.findings: Read the Arabic WAFA report dated 20 January 2026, specifically the meeting, attendance and Ashrawi remarks passages. It names her as Birzeit trustees chair, records actual participation and gives her comments on women’s affairs. This is direct recent-activity evidence rather than an upcoming invitation or an old biographical title. Statements by the minister or other participants are not transferred to Ashrawi; the report is not a court determination on the broader conflict. No meeting video was reviewed.

sources.title: Indexed university announcement: first woman trustees chair from 15 August 2023
sources.findings: Read indexed university announcement text confirming first-woman trustees chair and the 15 August 2023 start. The page body returned HTTP 403. A separate indexed university announcement identifies the election decision on 3 September 2022 and planned 15 August 2023 inauguration; distinguish decision from taking office. PalQuest and the readable January 2026 WAFA report independently support the chairmanship. University pages give inconsistent deanship end dates of 1993 and 1995, reinforcing the decision to leave the end year unspecified. Chair of the Board of Trustees is not president/rector of the university.

sources.title: 13 August 2026 indexed report: trustees chair discusses academic cooperation with Chinese ambassador
sources.findings: Read the indexed Arabic university report dated 13 August 2026. It identifies Ashrawi as trustees chair and says she met Chinese ambassador Sun Zhen and a delegation to discuss academic and institutional cooperation. The full page returned HTTP 403, so the dossier uses only the indexed event and office, not details beyond the excerpt, actual funding disbursements or completed medical-faculty projects. The university’s publication date is retained; no unseen recording or photo was used to certify appearance. January WAFA remains the directly read recent-activity evidence.

sources.title: Indexed institutional mission: December 1998 establishment and democratic governance
sources.findings: Read the indexed MIFTAH About Us mission excerpt, which gives establishment in Jerusalem in December 1998 and goals of democracy and good governance. The full page returned 502. AUB and AMAN independently corroborate Ashrawi’s founding role. No current secretary-general or executive-management title is asserted from the 2008 introduction, and mission statements are not audited outcomes.

portraitReview.unresolved: Read Commons description, date, source, author, licence and file history. Despite August in the filename, the description and date field identify the Anna Lindh memorial concert in Stockholm on 11 September 2013 at 18:53:24. The 27 April 2015 timestamp is the upload date. Original dimensions are 972×1280 and displayed file size is 1.23 MB; the old cache record of 167689 bytes is not proof of a downloaded original. DIFFswe is the uploader while Frankie Fouganthin is the credited creator. CC BY-SA 4.0 requires attribution, licence link, modification notice and share-alike for adaptations. Original download on 18 November returned curl 22, HTTP 403 and reported HTTP 000; the exact referenced local cache is absent. Identity, colour, crop, sharpness and original-byte correspondence have not been visually checked.
